item.title: 'Inside Gaza' wins best documentary at Montreal's Cinemania film festival
item.description:
"Inside Gaza," a documentary that follows journalists from global news agency AFP after the October 7, 2023 attack, received the Best Documentary Film award at Montreal's Cinemania Film Festival on Saturday.

Directed by Helene Lam Trong, the 72-minute film follows the daily lives of four AFP journalists who bear witness to the difficulties of reporting in a war-torn territory largely closed off to international media.

The film is compiled from material produced by the team on the ground, as well as from interviews conducted after they left.

item.title: McIlroy wins record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title
item.description:
Rory McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai title to tie the record of Scotland's Colin Montgomerie after a dramatic final round of the season-ending $10 million DP World Tour Championship on Sunday.

The tournament itself was a runaway win for England's Tyrrell Hatton (66) but all eyes were on the fascinating battle between McIlroy and Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, playing a group behind.

It all came down to the 18th hole, where McIlroy made a disappointing par to finish on 10-under par, but that was good enough for a solo second place.

item.title: Three men sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
item.description:
A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over a deadly church shooting, as the kingdom's Christmas celebrations were cancelled in solidarity with the victims' families.

Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Hammoud village, Karak governorate, on October 23.

item.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack
item.description:
AMMAN, Nov 15 (Reuters) - Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for carrying out an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported.

The court convicted the men of offences including carrying out terrorist acts resulting in death, possessing weapons and ammunition for terrorist purposes and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group. The ruling is subject to appeal and automatic review by the Court of Cassation, Petra said.

item.title: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi and Yomna Ehab

Nov 15 (Reuters) - Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, with the Israeli military confirming his death.

Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed on Saturday, said the Palestinian militant group's armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades.

item.title: Yemeni government force retreats from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
item.description:
By Mohammed Ghobari

Nov 15 (Reuters) - Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that squeezed oil exports.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province
item.description:
Nov 15 (Reuters) - The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province.

The Houthis, who control most of the populous parts of Yemen, have intensified attacks on the Saudi capital in recent days. A Houthi attack last week damaged an administrative building of the state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh's financial hub.

item.title: Scattered by war, the band that gave voice to Sudan's revolution plays again
item.description:
The Cairo studio where Sudanese musician Mohamed al-Mustafa strums his guitar is a long way away from the Khartoum protests where his band once performed for thousands demanding democracy, before war scattered them across multiple continents.

After living through revolution, war and years of displacement, Mustafa and his fellow musicians in "Aswat al-Madina" (Arabic for Voices of the City) have reunited in the Egyptian capital, returning to both recording and live performance.

item.title: Iran's navy says three tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
item.description:
Nov 14 (Reuters) - Iran's navy said three oil tankers caught fire on Saturday after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported.

One tanker hit a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Saturday morning, while two others struck mines later in the day.

"Two violating tankers ... were attempting to slip through a prohibited route in the Strait of Hormuz when they hit naval mines, exploded, and burst into flames," Iran's IRNA news agency quoted the Revolutionary Guards Navy as saying about the evening incident.

item.title: Netanyahu calls for Israeli unity government, Eisenkot dismisses 'tricks'
item.description:
Israel's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse.

The latest exchange comes as Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government, after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday.

item.title: Trump wagers time is on US side, for now, in dealing with Iran
item.description: The US can afford patience, but it should pair pressure with reassurance to its Middle Eastpartners.

item.title: UN official urges Iran, US to let fertilisers through Hormuz Strait
item.description:
Iran and the United States should "immediately" allow fertiliser shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to ease the crisis in some of the most vulnerable countries, a senior UN official said Saturday.

Jorge Moreira da Silva, head of the UN Office for Project Services, told the COP31 climate talks in the Turkish resort city of Antalya that the lack of fertilisers could push millions into poverty.

item.title: US floated idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskiy says
item.description:
By Olena Harmash

KYIV, Nov 14 (Reuters) - US negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine's potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, following the latest round of peace talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi.

This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, Zelenskiy said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday.

item.title: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
item.description:
By Erin Banco, Humeyra Pamuk, Phil Stewart and Timour Azhari

WASHINGTON/RIYADH, Nov 14 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump has told senior advisers in recent days that he may hold off onattacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, according to three people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Analysis-A new 'Yalta'? Trump and Putin push for a meeting that Xi is wary of hosting
item.description:
By Trevor Hunnicutt, Mei Mei Chu and Andrew Osborn

WASHINGTON/BEIJING/MOSCOW, Nov 14 (Reuters) - The world's three most powerful leaders could sit down together next week to discuss global flashpoints, from wars in Ukraine and Iran to nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence.

The prospects for any grand bargain emerging from the rare encounter, however, are slim.

item.title: UN climate chief urges speed as COP31 confronts fossil fuel divide
item.description:
By Simon Jessop and William James

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 14 (Reuters) - The UN's top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 conference in Turkey on Saturday to move swiftly towards a deal and "avoid tactical delays" as the summit heads into its second and final week.

The annual UN climate conference faces new challenges this year as a slew of crises from war to inflation push global warming down the list of priorities for world governments.

item.title: As smog hangs over Lahore, Pakistan's new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
item.description:
By Mubasher Bukhari

LAHORE, Nov 14 (Reuters) - As smog again settles over large parts of South Asia, Pakistani authorities are widening a crackdown on illegal stubble burning they say is fuelling the region's annual pollution crisis.

On Thursday, officers of a new quick-response unit swung off their vehicles at a paddy field on the edge of Lahore. Smoke curled low over the stubble, and the crew had the fire under control within minutes, keeping it fromadding to the haze over a city that Swiss group IQAir rated “very unhealthy” earlier this week.

item.title: 'A moral red line'? World on cusp of autonomous weapons revolution
item.description:
Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence are set to revolutionise warfare  but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology.

A conference starting Monday at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some.

But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons.

item.title: Trump to raise nuclear-arms cuts with Putin, Xi on Thursday, White House says
item.description:
By Trevor Hunnicutt and Jasper Ward

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will raise nuclear-arms reduction at a meeting in China next week with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President XiJinping, the White House said on Friday.

"He will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," Olivia Wales, a White House spokeswoman, said on a call with reporters. She added that the meeting would take place on Thursday in China.

item.title: ASEAN unity faces test as energy crisis, regional conflicts loom over summit
item.description:
By Nestor Corrales and Karen Lema

MANILA, Nov 14 (Reuters) - Southeast Asian foreign ministers begin meetings in Manila on Saturday as the regional bloc seeks a coordinated response to surging energy costs, security tensions, and an approaching ElNiño, challenges Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.has said demand collective action.
